items.title: FAA Orders Rare Nationwide Ground Stop Over Air Traffic Control Comms Issue
items.summary: This is only the third nationwide ground stop in 25 years. The last one, during a 2023 system outage, lasted about two hours.

items.title: Tripadvisor Reverses Merger of Experiences Teams, Cuts Cruise Critic Staff 60%: Scoop
items.summary: There's often a lot of hype about the strategic benefits in a restructuring. Tripadvisor admitted its November 2025 restructuring didn't work.

items.title: Beyond Miles: Earning Loyalty Through Proactive Care
items.summary: Airlines can expand the value of loyalty currencies by allowing travelers to redeem rewards for services beyond flights and upgrades.

items.title: How Airlines Can Own the Whole Trip in the AI Era
items.summary: Airlines have an opportunity to extend their customer relationships beyond flights as AI agents reshape travel planning and booking.

items.title: New Webinar: Turning Travel Disruptions Into Guest Loyalty
items.summary: This sponsored content was created in collaboration with a Skift partner. Travel is sold in pieces. Guests experience it as one trip. When a flight delay knocks out the connection, the first hotel night, and the plans after it, guests expect someone to help put it back together.

items.title: How Proactive AI Is Changing the Airline Customer Experience
items.summary: Airlines considering proactive AI agents face an implementation decision: how much responsibility should they give the technology before it has demonstrated reliable performance in routine customer service?

items.title: The Hotel Restaurant Is Becoming the Main Event Again
items.summary: Hotel restaurants are becoming destinations again. The smartest owners are giving chefs and operators the freedom to create places with their own character and following, rather than trying to serve every guest at every hour.

items.title: Saudi Hotel Builders Keep Going as Attacks Scare Off Foreign Visitors
items.summary: Saudi hotel developers are still building through Houthi attacks, and a record pipeline shows it. But their bet rests on domestic and religious travel. The international guests that Vision 2030 needs are the ones the attacks are scaring off.
